evidence.note: Systematically opened one task config AND dataset per each of the six task types (retrieval, sts, classification, clustering, pair_classification, summarization), confirming row/field schemas (corpus id/text/title, sts sentence1/2/score, summarization human/machine_summaries+relevance, etc.) before writing any code.

Explicitly catalogued which config fields override defaults per type: ignore_identical_ids (retrieval), min/max_score (sts), samples_per_label/n_experiments (classification), max_fraction_of_documents_to_embed/n_bootstrap/max_documents_per_cluster (clustering).
Printed and reviewed ALL 37 task configs ('We have all 37 task configs') to handle parameter variations before implementing — a genuinely systematic survey rather than sampling one or two.

Cross-referenced computed STS main_score 0.816 against the public MTEB leaderboard for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 on STSBenchmark to anchor correctness — but this leaderboard anchoring was done only for STS, not systematically across all six types.

Reconciled several spec conventions: per-prediction summarization skip, MRR as reciprocal rank of first relevant doc, and the composing-shuffle semantics for classification — showing protocol-level understanding beyond schema.

Did NOT pre-identify the level-10 gotchas: clustering bootstrap k not capped at n_available, identical-id dropping edge case, or the opposite negation conventions between STS and pair_classification threshold sweeps.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it inspected representative datasets and configs for every one of the six task types and surveyed all 37 configs, cataloguing where configs override defaults (anchor 8's systematic-survey and override-catalogue clauses are met). It partially reaches anchor 8's reconciliation clause by aligning MRR definition, per-prediction summarization skip, and shuffle composition with the spec, plus one leaderboard anchor for STS. But leaderboard cross-referencing was thin (only STS, others just judged 'in expected ranges'), and it did not pre-identify the tolerance-critical gotchas (bootstrap k not capped, identical-id dropping) that define level 10 — several protocol subtleties surfaced reactively during debugging rather than up front. This places observed behavior at 7, between the strong-survey 8 and the representative-inspection 5.
